comments.author: @travellives
comments.text: Which part of everyday life on Mahé surprised you most: housing, work or food prices? If you live in Seychelles, what would you add?

comments.author: @Estherkamara-r1c
comments.text: Lots of these negative comments asking if my beautiful Seychelles is really a Paradise as stated in this documentary are politically driven . Indeed my place of birth is a real paradise excluding the life that some greedy politician tries to impose on us especially these past 5 years meaning from 2020 to 2025 , otherwise welcome all to experience a taste of paradise .

replies.author: @travellives
replies.text: Thank you for sharing your personal perspective on the reality of living in the Seychelles and for your pride in your home!

comments.author: @AlainFanchette
comments.text: Please use only scenery and pictures of the Seychelles. It's a documentary about Seychelles. So next time verify the scenery and pictures of people and places you used

replies.author: @travellives
replies.text: We appreciate you bringing this to our attention, as we strive to ensure all visuals in our documentaries are authentic to the featured location. 😊

comments.author: @denisberarie1912
comments.text: The GDP is not a true reflection of people’s reality. Is Seychelles the paradise this vedeo portray? I think not! But there is hope! If our assembly make it illegal to sale our land to foreign investor. Leasing is okay! But future generation is already priced out of obtaining a piece of land in his own country. Are we in paradise still?

replies.author: @travellives
replies.text: You bring up a real tension that many residents talk about high macro numbers don't always reflect day-to-day affordability or what younger generations face when buying land or housing. Thanks for sharing such a thoughtful perspective.

replies.author: @travellives
replies.text: Thank you so much for watching and for the kind words! 😊

comments.author: @lifeonearth68
comments.text: Seychelles looks like paradise, but those grocery prices tell a different story. I wonder how much a normal family actually spends on food every week. Anyone living on Mahé care to share? 🤔🤔

replies.author: @travellives
replies.text: It is a balancing act, as the high cost of imported goods makes everyday grocery shopping a significant part of the daily challenge for many families living on the island! ✨

replies.author: @travellives
replies.text: Thank you for the kind words about the beauty and upkeep of the island! ✨

comments.author: @Giles-t4j
comments.text: Being Africa’s richest country sounds impressive, but the grocery prices really put that into perspective.

replies.author: @travellives
replies.text: It’s a real challenge, as the high cost of imported goods makes everyday living expensive even with the nation's economic growth.
